edges.description: Carries the most common human RP13 allele in the endogenous gene and develops late RPE degeneration and reduced RPE phagocytosis.
edges.limitations: The early phagocytosis defect was measured in homozygous mice, and heterozygotes, the human genotype, show only late RPE morphological change at about two years. The mouse does not develop the photoreceptor degeneration that defines the human disease, and patient iPSC-RPE did not reproduce its phagocytosis defect.

evidence.reference_title: Autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa with intrafamilial variability and incomplete penetrance in two families carrying mutations in PRPF8.
evidence.snippet: mild rod dysfunction on scotopic electroretinography (ERG)

nodes.description: In patient iPSC-derived retinal cells carrying H2309P, weak 5' splice sites are used less, cryptic splicing increases, and the changes fall mainly on ciliary and retina-specific transcripts. Other RP13 variants reduce PRPF8 binding to pre-mRNA and slow intron removal in RPE cells.

evidence.reference_title: PRPF8-mediated dysregulation of hBrr2 helicase disrupts human spliceosome kinetics and 5´-splice-site selection causing tissue-specific defects.
evidence.snippet: for which disruption impaired alternative splicing and weak/suboptimal 5'SS selection, and enhanced cryptic splicing, predominantly in ciliary and retinal-specific transcripts

evidence.reference_title: Retinitis pigmentosa-linked mutations impair the snRNA unwinding activity of SNRNP200 and reduce pre-mRNA binding of PRPF8.
evidence.snippet: The RP variants of PRPF8 did not affect snRNAs, but showed a reduced binding to pre-mRNAs, which resulted in the slower splicing of introns and altered expression of hundreds of genes in RPE cells.

evidence.reference_title: Clinical characterization, linkage analysis, and PRPC8 mutation analysis of a family with autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa type 13 (RP13).
evidence.snippet: a diffuse loss of rod and cone sensitivity, and constricted visual fields (type I)

nodes.description: The PRPF8 C-terminal tail normally inserts into the RNA-binding tunnel of the Brr2 helicase and represses it until U4/U6 unwinding is due. RP13 variants weaken that repression and the PRPF8-Brr2 interaction, disturbing U5 snRNP maturation, spliceosome activation and the transition between the two catalytic steps, and lowering overall splicing efficiency.
nodes.id: Impaired Regulation of the Brr2 Helicase

biological_processes: Brr2-driven U4/U6 release during spliceosome activation

evidence.reference_title: Inhibition of RNA helicase Brr2 by the C-terminal tail of the spliceosomal protein Prp8.
evidence.snippet: Inefficient Brr2 repression is the only recognizable phenotype associated with certain retinitis pigmentosa-linked Prp8 mutations that map to its C-terminal tail.

evidence.reference_title: prp8 mutations that cause human retinitis pigmentosa lead to a U5 snRNP maturation defect in yeast.
evidence.snippet: RP mutations in Prp8p in yeast result in nuclear accumulation of the precursor U5 snRNP, apparently as a consequence of disrupting the interaction of Prp8p with Brr2p.

evidence.reference_title: Prp8 retinitis pigmentosa mutants cause defects in the transition between the catalytic steps of splicing.
evidence.snippet: Though Prp8-RP mutants do not cause defects in splicing fidelity, they result in an overall decrease in splicing efficiency.

nodes.description: Most variants are missense changes clustered in the last exons of PRPF8, in the C-terminal region that regulates the Brr2 helicase; H2309P is the best-characterized allele. Nonsense variants in the same region are also reported and are predicted to escape nonsense-mediated decay. Some alleles outside the last exon, such as T1931M, lower PRPF8 levels in patient RPE, so reduced dosage may contribute for those.

evidence.reference_title: Mutations in the pre-mRNA splicing factor gene PRPC8 in autosomal dominant retinitis pigmentosa (RP13).
evidence.snippet: The seven mutations are clustered within a 14 codon stretch within the last exon of this large 7 kb transcript.

evidence.reference_title: PRPF8 / PRPF8-related retinopathy (Definitive)
evidence.snippet: Nonsense variants have also been associated with disease; it is predicted that C-terminal stop mutations may escape nonsense mediated decay

evidence.reference_title: PRPF8-mediated dysregulation of hBrr2 helicase disrupts human spliceosome kinetics and 5´-splice-site selection causing tissue-specific defects.
evidence.snippet: The carboxy-terminus of the spliceosomal protein PRPF8, which regulates the RNA helicase Brr2, is a hotspot for mutations causing retinitis pigmentosa-type 13

nodes.description: Photoreceptors show ciliary and polarity defects and outer segment thinning, and rods are lost before cones. In retinal organoids these defects arise in the neural retina without RPE, so they are not only secondary to RPE failure. The cilium assembly binding is inferred from the reported ciliary defects; the sources do not show which step of ciliogenesis fails.

evidence.reference_title: PRPF8-mediated dysregulation of hBrr2 helicase disrupts human spliceosome kinetics and 5´-splice-site selection causing tissue-specific defects.
evidence.snippet: We used patient induced pluripotent stem cells-derived cells, carrying the heterozygous PRPF8 c.6926 A > C (p.H2309P) mutation to demonstrate retinal-specific endophenotypes comprising photoreceptor loss, apical-basal polarity and ciliary defects.

evidence.reference_title: PRPF8-associated retinitis pigmentosa variant induces human neural retina-autonomous photoreceptor defects.
evidence.snippet: Together, we present a model of RP that recapitulates photoreceptor degeneration and demonstrates that these defects are independent of RPE degeneration.

evidence.reference_title: Histologic study of retinitis pigmentosa due to a mutation in the RP13 gene (PRPC8): comparison with rhodopsin Pro23His, Cys110Arg, and Glu181Lys.
evidence.snippet: All eyes showed loss of rod photoreceptors.

nodes.description: Patient iPSC-derived RPE carrying a PRPF8 variant shows weakened barrier function, disrupted polarity, loss of apical microvilli and pigment granules, and splicing changes enriched in cilium and melanosome pathways, all reversed by base-editing correction. In Prpf8 H2309P knock-in mice, primary RPE from homozygous animals phagocytoses less at a young age, and heterozygous RPE degenerates morphologically by two years. Another patient iPSC-RPE line phagocytosed normally, so how much RPE failure contributes in patients is unresolved.
